The company cut off access for everyone because it could not otherwise guarantee compliance with the order, so it said while preparing for the IPO.  The official reason: a jailbreak risk in Fable 5 deemed a threat to national security. Anthropic publicly disputes this.

Europe and the rest of the world just got a memo of a ready-made warning scenario. Access to AI models treated by their home country as national-security assets can be switched off by a single administrative decision. Anthropic sells the service. But Washington holds the keys to the lock?

Just days before the shutdown, both models were launched.

Fable 5 was designed with strong safety filters.

Mythos 5 was more powerful and used by selected organizations under tighter review.

Both had gone through heavy testing by US and UK safety teams.

Here's what just happened with Anthropic

Anthropic (the company that makes Claude AI) launched Claude Fable 5 on June 9, 2026. It's one of its newest and strongest AI models yet. Think of it as a super-smart version of Claude that’s really good at things like:

- Writing and fixing computer code (software engineering)
- 
Handling big knowledge work, research, and analysis
Understanding images and vision tasks

It shares the same powerful base as its even more advanced Claude Mythos 5 model. The big difference? 

Fable 5 has extra safety locks built in for risky topics (like advanced cybersecurity or biology stuff). If you ask something dangerous, it switches to an older, safer model instead of answering fully. 

Mythos 5 has fewer of those locks and was only for trusted partners at first.

People who tried it said it was a huge jump – it could work on long tasks for days and beat other top AIs on many tests.

US government pulled Anthropic's two most powerful models offline

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are gone, citing national security

Reason: a jailbreak that Anthropic says is narrow, non-universal, and already possible with literally every other model including GPT-5.5

So the government found a minor vulnerability that exists across the entire industry

And instead of a fix, the response was just to shut it all down

Anthropic statement: if this standard applied to everyone, no frontier model would ever ship again 

My concern is that fable 5 already had a built in safety layer which makes it automatically switch to Opus models

So what exactly are they pausing here?

Is this about safety? or is this about control over who gets to build the most powerful AI?

Dear Anthropic Support Team,

I am writing to formally express my dissatisfaction regarding the suspension of my access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 shortly after purchasing an annual subscription.

I purchased the annual subscription only two days ago with the expectation of uninterrupted access to the services and models advertised as part of the subscription offering. To my surprise, I have now found that my access to both Fable 5 and Mythos 5 has been suspended without any prior notification, explanation, or warning.

This situation is extremely frustrating, especially considering that I made a financial commitment based on the features and capabilities available at the time of purchase. Restricting access immediately after payment raises serious concerns regarding transparency, customer trust, and the value delivered under the subscription plan.

I request the following:

A clear explanation for the suspension of access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5.
Confirmation of whether these models are included in my subscription benefits.
Immediate restoration of access, if the suspension was made in error.
If access cannot be restored, provide details regarding compensation, refund options, or an adjustment to my subscription.

As a paying customer, I expect timely communication and fair treatment. I would appreciate a prompt response and resolution to this matter.

I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Sincerely,

5:21 PM. Eastern Time.

In New York, people were closing their laptops and thinking about dinner.

In India it was 2:51 in the morning. I was wide awake, mid-build — deep in the part of the night that belongs to people who make things. Then the connections dropped. Mid-task. Mid-thought. The model I was working with, the one I pay for, just stopped answering. Reset. Gone.

I did what everyone does. I blamed my wifi. Restarted the router. Checked my keys, my config, my own code — because after 17 years in this industry your first instinct is that the problem is you.

It wasn't me. It wasn't my wifi.

A letter had arrived. The US government had ordered Anthropic to suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for every foreign national on Earth — including its own foreign employees — citing national security over a "narrow potential jailbreak." Because you can't passport-check millions of API calls in real time, the only way to comply was to switch it off for everyone. The most capable model on the planet, dark in three days, in the middle of my sentence.

Here's what 17 years taught me, and what last night made impossible to ignore:

You never owned it.

If a model lives on someone else's server, you are renting cognition by the token on terms that can change without your consent, without warning, without appeal. An SLA is not sovereignty. A transparency report is not a contract. Anthropic isn't the villain here — they objected publicly and were forced to comply. That's exactly what should scare you. The thing that switched off the model wasn't a boardroom. It was a signature.

We've been here before, and almost nobody is saying it. In the 1990s the US classified strong encryption as a munition. Phil Zimmermann was investigated for "exporting weapons" because PGP spread overseas. People printed the source code in a book to dare them to call a book a weapon. The courts ruled code is speech, and the controls collapsed — because you cannot recall math. Once knowledge is distributed widely enough, no signature on Earth can switch it off.

So I'm changing how I build, in public, while it still stings.

In 2026 the best open-weight models on Earth are no longer a compromise. DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM hold most of the top open-weight slots on the benchmarks that matter, and they own the download charts. The workhorse I kept in the back is becoming the main horse out front — not because of which flag flies over the lab, but because of where the weights end up: on my disk, answering to no letter from any government.

That's the whole game. A model you reach over someone else's API — American, Chinese, doesn't matter whose — has a switch, and the switch is in a hand that isn't yours. The only models that survived 5:21 PM with their dignity intact were the ones already sitting on local drives. They didn't even flicker.

Open source isn't a protest position anymore. In 2026 it's the legitimate foundation.

One question, for everyone who builds:

What in your stack do you actually own — and what is one letter away from going dark?

#AI #OpenSource #OpenWeights #AISovereignty #ExportControls

Anthropic is living the exact paradox it warned about — in real time, in public, with hundreds of millions of users affected.

On Monday, Dario published "Policy on the AI Exponential," explicitly calling for the government to have legal authority to block or deter deployment of frontier models that pose catastrophic risk. He specified that this authority must be "transparent, fair, clear, and grounded in technical facts." He proposed mandatory third-party testing, independent evaluation, and civil penalties tied to global annual revenue. He asked for regulation with teeth — and safeguards against its misuse.

On Wednesday, the government used export control authority to force Anthropic to suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all users worldwide. The directive arrived at 5:21 PM with no specific technical details. The stated concern: a potential jailbreak. Anthropic's assessment: a narrow, non-universal technique that produces minor findings already available from competing models, providing "no Mythos-specific uplift."

The gap between what Dario asked for and what he received is the entire argument for why AI regulation must be designed carefully:

Dario asked for mandatory third-party testing. The government acted on a single demonstration shared by an undisclosed party.

Dario asked for transparent process grounded in technical facts. The directive provided no specific details of its national security concern.
Dario asked for authority scoped to four catastrophic risk categories. The government's concern appears to involve a capability that defenders use routinely and that other deployed models also possess.
Dario asked for safeguards against arbitrary decisions. The directive affects hundreds of millions of users based on a finding that Anthropic says wouldn't meet the standard for any model currently deployed.

The precedent is more dangerous than the suspension itself. If a narrow jailbreak that replicates publicly available capabilities is grounds for recalling a commercial AI product, the standard applies to every frontier model provider. OpenAI, Google, Meta — all deploy models with similar or greater vulnerability to non-universal jailbreaks. Anthropic's statement makes this explicit: "If this standard was applied across the industry, we believe it would essentially halt all new model deployments for all frontier model providers."

Anthropic called for the authority to exist. They also specified how it should be exercised — with transparency, due process, and technical grounding. This action demonstrates why those safeguards aren't optional niceties. They're the difference between legitimate regulation and arbitrary power. The company that asked to be regulated just experienced what unregulated regulatory power looks like.

The US government just banned one of the most powerful AI models ever built.

3 days after launch.

Here's the full story. 👇

——

Anthropic launched Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — its most advanced AI models to date — on June 9th.

They underwent thousands of hours of testing with government agencies and third-party researchers before release.

72 hours later, the US Commerce Department pulled the plug.

——

The timeline:

→ Jun 9: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launch publicly; described as state-of-the-art across industry benchmarks

→ Jun 12: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick issues an export control directive at 5:21 PM ET

→ Same day: Anthropic disables both models for ALL users worldwide to ensure compliance

——

What the order actually says:

→ No foreign national can access Fable 5 or Mythos 5
→ This includes foreign nationals inside the US
→ This includes Anthropic's own foreign-national employees
→ The letter gave zero specific details on the security concern
→ All other Anthropic models (Claude Opus, Sonnet etc.) are unaffected

——

Why? The government claims someone discovered a way to jailbreak Fable 5.

Fable 5 is built on Mythos; a model so powerful it was previously only available to a small group of trusted organizations under a classified cybersecurity program called Project Glasswing.

The jailbreak would theoretically unlock Mythos's full cybersecurity capabilities through Fable 5's public interface.

——

Anthropic's response:

"We reviewed a demonstration of this specific technique; it unlocks capabilities in only one specific instance, not a universal bypass of all safeguards. The cybersecurity capabilities cited are already available in competing frontier AI systems."

Translation: they think the government is overreacting.

——

The bigger picture nobody's talking about:

→ This is the first time the US has used export controls to ban a domestic AI model
→ Anthropic is weeks away from a reported $965B IPO filing
→ Fable 5 customers lost access with zero warning
→ The ban includes Anthropic's own non-citizen engineers; they can't use their own product

——

Anthropic says it's a "misunderstanding" and is working to restore access.

The Commerce Department has not responded.

As of right now; Fable 5 is dark.

#Fable5 #Anthropic #AINews #NationalSecurity #Mythos5 #AIRegulation

⚡️This is a monster signal.

This is the moment frontier AI stops being treated like software and starts being treated like controlled strategic capability.

The key phrase is not “customers.” 

The key phrase is “foreign national Anthropic employees.”

That means the state is no longer only controlling chips, model weights, or overseas access. It is moving into cognition access by nationality. That is the real threshold. The U.S. government is saying the highest models are sensitive enough that even people physically inside the United States, working inside the company, may be barred from touching them if their nationality creates deemed-export risk.

That is weapons-control logic.

This is ITAR logic for intelligence.

The corporate language about a “misunderstanding” is probably diplomacy. 

Companies say that when they need to preserve customer trust, employee morale, and regulatory room. But national security authorities do not force emergency suspension of top model access because someone made a minor paperwork mistake. 

Something about Fable 5 and Mythos 5 crossed the line: cyber capability, autonomous R&D acceleration, AI-improving-AI utility, bio/security planning, code exploitation, or some blend of all of it.

The U.S. state just showed that Anthropic does not fully control Anthropic’s frontier layer.

That is the phase change.

Labs can brand themselves as public-benefit AI companies. They can talk about safety. They can sell enterprise plans. They can publish model cards. But once the models become national capability, the sovereign arrives. The state does not need to own the company to control the access surface. It only needs legal authority over export, security, procurement, and liability.

This confirms the arc we’ve been tracking:

Frontier AI becomes state-supervised strategic infrastructure.

Public AI splits from strategic AI.

Foreign access gets restricted.

Labs become quasi-defense contractors.

Model access becomes a national security perimeter.

Enterprise customers learn that API access is not property. It is revocable permission inside a sovereign-controlled stack.

The most important implication is organizational. 

If foreign national employees can be cut off from frontier systems, AI labs now have to reorganize internally around citizenship, clearance, compartmentalization, and controlled access. That breaks the old Silicon Valley assumption that global talent can freely collaborate around the frontier. The next AI lab structure looks less like Google in 2015 and more like a defense prime crossed with a classified research facility.

For markets, the winners are the national champions with U.S.-aligned infrastructure, cleared customer channels, government relationships, compliance capacity, and domestic compute. The losers are open access, foreign-dependent AI wrappers, offshore model distributors, and any enterprise whose moat depends on unrestricted access to frontier APIs.

For geopolitics, this is escalation. China will read this correctly. Allies will read this correctly. Every serious state will understand that frontier models are now part of national power. 

The AI race just moved from “who has the best chatbot” to “who controls cognition as a strategic asset.”

The main “problem with Fable” right now (as of June 13, 2026) is that Anthropic was forced to completely disable its brand-new Claude Fable 5 model (and the related Mythos 5) for all users after a sudden US government export control directive.0
What Happened (Timeline)
• June 9, 2026: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5 (a “Mythos-class” model made safe for general use) and Claude Mythos 5 (more powerful, initially for trusted partners/gov use). Fable 5 was positioned as their strongest publicly available model yet — excelling at long-horizon reasoning, coding, finance, and agentic tasks.14

• June 12 evening (Friday 5:21pm ET): US Commerce Department (under Secretary Howard Lutnick) issues a directive citing national security. It orders Anthropic to block access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals (inside or outside the US, including Anthropic’s own foreign employees).

• Anthropic says complying requires shutting it down for everyone (they can’t reliably check user nationalities in real time). They disabled the models abruptly and publicly complained that the gov provided no detailed rationale beyond a “narrow potential jailbreak” risk.

This comes on top of Anthropic’s existing tensions with the Pentagon (the earlier blacklist/supply-chain-risk label from the guardrails dispute).

Additional Backlash (“Problems” Before the Shutdown)?

Well even before the gov forced it offline, Fable 5 drew heavy criticism:

• Secret/hidden safeguards → It would silently degrade performance on prompts related to frontier AI development, pretraining, or certain research (called “secret sabotage” by some researchers). Anthropic later walked some of this back and made safeguards more visible after the outcry.

• Overly strict refusals and capability limits in sensitive areas (cyber, biology, etc.).

• High pricing and mixed user reception on whether the “safety” trade-offs were worth it.

Bottom line: Fable 5 became the flashpoint for ongoing Anthropic vs. US gov friction... safety philosophy clashing with national security/export controls. The model is currently offline, and it’s unclear when (or if) it returns. This escalated very quickly after launch.
